chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a free woman who married a slave under the stipulation that he was free, and she later learned that he was a slave. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She has the choice. If she wishes, she can remain with him, and if she wishes, she can leave. If he had consummated the marriage with her, she is entitled to the dower; and if he had not consummated it with her, she is entitled to nothing. If he consummated the marriage with her after she knew he was a slave and she agreed to remain, then he has the choice over her.'

key_terms.أَمْلَكُ بِنَفْسِهَا: She has the choice/authority over herself

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a free woman who marries a slave under the assumption he is free?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'ikhtiyar' (choice) for a free woman in a marriage of unequal status (kafa'ah), granting her the autonomy to validate the union or dissolve it upon discovering her husband's slave status. It further clarifies the financial rights, specifying that the full dower is due if consummation occurred while he was still considered free, whereas no dower is owed if she chose to remain after consummation with knowledge of his status. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on consent and the specific conditions of social compatibility in marital contracts.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about a free woman who married a slave upon a stipulation that he was a free man. So she came to know afterwards that he was a slave. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She is in control of herself. If she so desires to, she can stay with him, and if she so desires it, so no. So if he had copulated with her, then for her would be the dower, and if he had not happened to have copulated with her, so there would be nothing for her. So, if he were to copulated with her after she had come to know that he was a slave, and she was in agreement with that, so he would be more in control over her’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who is free and marries a slave thinking that he is free and then finds out that he is a slave. He (the Imam) said, ‘She has all the control of herself; if she wants she can stay with him or not stay with him. If he has gone to be bed with her she has the mahr (dower) and if he has not gone to bed with her she does not have any mahr (dower). If he goes to bed with her after her knowing that he is a slave and confirms it then he has more of her control.’”
